note: Every difficulty rating, time estimate and tip in this file is this guide's own work, reasoned out from the official trophy descriptions alone — PlayStation publishes no difficulty or time for any trophy, so none of these numbers come from PlayStation. The counts and grades belong to the official list (Exophase and PSNProfiles). An 'avoid' line appears only beside a missable trophy, and it names the one concrete habit that keeps that trophy safe. Each entry also names the roadmap stage it belongs to, so the detail pane can say where the trophy sits on the road to the platinum.

notes.tip: Do not chase this one directly. Work the roadmap stages in order, tick each trophy off as it pops, and this platinum lands on its own the moment the other 54 are done.

notes.avoid: Play the opening mission from its start to its end screen in one sitting — quitting halfway means starting the mission over.
notes.tip: Take the fishing mission the moment the story offers it and play it through to the end screen. The trophy fires on completion, so treat the mission as one unbroken run.

notes.avoid: Finish every Chapter 1 mission before the story carries you into Chapter 2 — a chapter trophy only fires while you are still in that chapter.
notes.tip: Play Chapter 1 to its close without skipping its missions. When the chapter-end screen appears, check this trophy off — it pops with the chapter, not with any single mission.

notes.avoid: Work through Chapter 2 in order and do not rush past its missions to reach the next chapter — the trophy belongs to the chapter, not to one mission.
notes.tip: Keep playing the story in order until Chapter 2 closes. If a mission fails, retry it at once from the mission-failed screen rather than wandering off into free roam.

notes.avoid: Clear Chapter 3's missions as the story hands them to you — leaving one unfinished while you explore risks forgetting it when the chapter turns.
notes.tip: Stay with the story through Chapter 3 and finish each mission it offers before taking a long free-roam break. The chapter trophy pops when the last of its missions is done.

notes.avoid: Play Chapter 4 to its end before touching the final mission — the chapter trophy and the finale are separate pops, and the chapter comes first.
notes.tip: Finish Chapter 4 in story order and watch for the chapter-close pop. Do the chapter's missions back to back in one or two sessions so none of them slips your mind.

notes.avoid: When the final mission appears, play it to its end screen — do not quit or switch to free roam with the finale waiting.
notes.tip: Stock up before the finale, then play the final mission straight through. It is the gold trophy of the story, so give it a fresh session and your full attention.

notes.avoid: Take Breakfast Run the first time the story offers it and finish it in that same session — named missions do not wait around.
notes.tip: When Breakfast Run shows up in the story, go straight to its marker and play it to completion. Named-mission trophies fire on the mission's end screen, so do not leave mid-mission.

notes.avoid: Start The Cartel Heist when the story offers it and see it through to the end — a heist left half-done is a trophy left unpopped.
notes.tip: Prepare before the heist — a full stock of supplies and a clear session — then run the mission from start to finish. Retry at once from the fail screen if it goes wrong.

notes.avoid: Play Child's Play when it is offered and finish it before moving on to the next story beat.
notes.tip: Head to the mission marker as soon as Child's Play appears and play it through to its end screen. If you fail a section, retry immediately rather than leaving the mission hanging.

notes.avoid: Do Headliners in the session the story offers it — named missions are one-shot chances, not repeatable errands.
notes.tip: Take Headliners the moment it is offered and play it to the end. Keep a save from just before the mission, so a bad run costs you a retry, not the trophy.

notes.avoid: Start VCIA Takedown when offered and play it to completion in the same session — do not park it while you do side content.
notes.tip: Go to the VCIA Takedown marker as soon as it appears and run the mission straight through. The trophy pops on the end screen, so finish what you start.

notes.avoid: Play Operation Savage Glory to its end screen the first time it is offered — late-story missions are the easiest to leave behind.
notes.tip: Treat Operation Savage Glory like a finale: a fresh session, supplies topped up, and no free-roam detours until the end screen shows and the trophy pops.

notes.time: 60–70 hours, near the end of the guide
notes.tip: Chase this one last among the big goals. Finish the story, close every stranger strand, then open the game's completion list and clear whatever it still shows — the gold pops when that list hits 100%.
Spread the 250 stunts across your free-roam sessions instead of grinding them in one sitting. Chain small stunts — jumps, near misses, air time — and watch the counter climb in the stats menu.
Try one of each activity type the game offers — a race, a fishing spot, the range, the arcade — and tick each type off as you sample it. The trophy only asks you to try each kind once.

Work one weapon at a time and learn its challenge before chasing gold on it. Retry a single challenge until the gold medal lands, then move to the next weapon — do not hop between weapons mid-session.
Race drones at one location until you win there, then move to the next location on the list. Keep a note of which locations you have already won, and finish the last one the same way.
Enter a different race event each time rather than replaying one favourite — the trophy counts 20 different wins. Vary the event and the vehicle class to keep the wins coming.

notes.time: About an hour at the water
notes.tip: Take the fishing challenge against Cal and play it patiently — watch the line, reel steadily, and do not rush the catch. If you lose, challenge him again straight away.
Walk into an arcade, pick any game, and play it to its end screen. Any completed arcade game counts, so choose the shortest one you enjoy and finish it.

notes.avoid: Follow Andy's strand to its last mission and play that finale the moment it appears — a strand left one mission short is a trophy missed.
notes.tip: Check the map for Andy's marker whenever you are in free roam, and answer each of his missions in turn. When the final mission shows, play it through to its end screen.

notes.avoid: Keep Kenton's strand moving and play its final mission as soon as it is offered — do not leave a stranger strand hanging into the endgame.
notes.tip: Work Kenton's missions in the order they appear and keep his marker on your route. The finale pops its trophy on completion, so finish the strand before the story's final stretch.

notes.avoid: Finish Billy's strand before the endgame — a finale left undone when the story closes is the easiest trophy to lose.
notes.tip: Take Billy's missions whenever his marker appears and do not let the strand stall. Play the final mission in one sitting, from its start to its end screen.
Treat the eight stranger strands as one checklist: open each strand, finish it to its final mission, and tick it off. The silver pops when the eighth strand closes — half-finished strands stall it.

notes.avoid: Play Randy's final mission the moment it is offered and see it through — stranger finales do not repeat.
notes.tip: Follow Randy's strand mission by mission and answer his final call promptly. If the finale fails, retry it at once from the fail screen.

notes.avoid: Close Tyrone's strand before the endgame — play its final mission in the session it appears.
notes.tip: Keep Tyrone's marker in view while you roam and take each of his missions as it comes. The final mission's end screen is where the trophy pops.
Sweep the map region by region and meditate at each spot you find, marking it off as you go. A slow pass across Leonida catches the spots a fast drive would miss.

notes.time: About an hour on the hunt
notes.tip: Take Bret's hunt when it is offered and follow the trail it gives you — track, approach quietly, and take the shot only when the animal is clearly in view.

Collect cards in sets, not at random: pick one set, hunt its cards across the map, and finish it before starting the next. Check the collection menu after each find so you know which cards are still missing.
WAiNK It one location at a time while you travel for other trophies — snap a spot whenever you pass one, and keep a running count so the last ten do not become a separate grind.
Let the 50 challenges accumulate naturally — try new activities as they appear and the counter fills itself. Near the end, open the challenges list and clear the easiest ones still undone.

notes.avoid: Keep your partner beside you and the wanted level at four stars, then drive the escape together — splitting up or dropping the heat early voids the attempt.
notes.tip: Start the escape with your partner already in the car and four stars on the meter, then lose the heat together — break line of sight, change vehicles, and do not stop until the stars clear.

notes.avoid: Rob three shops in a row without letting the wanted level drop between them — one lost star between robberies breaks the streak.
notes.tip: Plan a short route past three shops, rob the first, and drive straight to the next two while the wanted level holds. Keep the route short so the heat never has time to fade.
Drive something new whenever you get the chance — hop into unfamiliar vehicles in traffic and on the roadside. The counter rewards variety, so a different car each trip beats one favourite.
Wait for a spot where five enemies group up, trigger Combat Focus, and take them down in that single use — one at a time will not count. If the group scatters, back off and set the attempt up again.

notes.avoid: When the unscheduled departure opens at VCIA, take it at once — the description ties it to a single moment, and the airport will not offer it twice.
notes.tip: Head to VCIA when the chance appears and make the departure without detours — get to the aircraft and leave. Do not stop to explore the airport first.
Take the Rhino somewhere open and get comfortable with how it handles before you try anything fancy — the trophy is about the tank, so give it a clear run and a little patience.
Scout the jewelry store first — watch its layout and its sightlines — then go in quiet and leave the same way. One detection ends the attempt, so plan the exit before you enter.
Rob one vault at a time and escape cleanly before starting the next — a clean escape after each vault keeps the count moving. Keep a getaway vehicle ready before you go in.
Pick an armored truck on a quiet stretch of road, hit it fast, and drive the escape route you planned before the robbery. The trophy pops once you are clear, not when the truck opens.
Explore one region at a time and check the map as you go — the trophy wants the whole state, so a methodical sweep beats fast travel. Leave the far corners for a dedicated road trip near the end.
Rob one illegal operation per gang, ticking each gang off as you go. Keep a list of which gangs you have hit so the last one does not send you hunting blind.

notes.avoid: When you are on Ocean Beach with the moment in front of you, take the cocktail there and then — it is a single free-roam moment, not a repeatable errand.
notes.tip: Walk the beach until the cocktail moment presents itself, then enjoy it with the view. Do it while you are passing Ocean Beach for other reasons — do not leave it for after the story.

notes.avoid: Drive into the showroom and smash your way out in the same visit — leaving calmly and coming back later will not count.
notes.tip: Enter the vehicle showroom, then make your exit the dramatic way the description suggests — straight through, in classic style. Commit to the smash in that one visit.

notes.avoid: Play the full game at the Kolt & Associates bowling alley when you are there — a partial game or a walk-away does not count.
notes.tip: Go to the bowling alley, start a full game, and follow through to its end. The trophy is about finishing the game, so stay at the lane until the last frame.
Build the partnership steadily — take on the activities that grow it and check the partnership's progress now and then. It pops when the partnership reaches its mark, so keep working at it.

notes.avoid: At the choice moment, stop and think before you pick — the description ties this trophy to choices made, and a rushed pick cannot be taken back.
notes.tip: When the story offers its choice, pause and consider it before deciding — the trophy follows the choice you make. If you are unsure, save first so a wrong pick costs a reload, not the trophy.

notes.avoid: When the first attempt fails, try again right away in the same place — the second attempt is the one that counts, and the moment passes if you walk off.
notes.tip: Fail once, then go again immediately — the trophy's name says the second time is the charm. Do not change location or activity between the two attempts.

notes.avoid: When the strange event happens, stay with it until it plays out — walking away mid-event ends the moment.
notes.tip: Keep your eyes open while roaming — when something strange happens, follow it to its end instead of driving past. The event is one-off, so curiosity pays here.
Take a melee weapon to the bowling alley and bowl them over with a drive-by — line the shot up from the car and commit to it. A few practice passes help before the real attempt.
Launder Marked Bills in steady batches through your contacts and watch the total climb — the $250,000 target is a sum, so small regular launders beat one risky haul.

Spend across many shops rather than one — buy gear, clothes and supplies as you go and the $100,000 total builds itself. Check the spending total now and then so the last stretch is not a blind splurge.
Buy garage properties one at a time as the money comes in, and keep a list of which ones you own. The trophy pops when the last garage is bought, so do not leave one forgotten.
Register vehicles to the Scooter Bros app as you find them — ten registrations, one at a time. Use the cars you drive every day so the count grows without a separate grind.
